Business goal: Allow a root admin to inspect branding state for exactly one selected tenant.
Tenant context rule: Root request identifies one selected tenant; cross-tenant ambiguity denies.
Authorization summary: Root actor must hold tenant branding read capability for the selected tenant.
Request contract: Exact tenant id route param; no body; clients cannot request deleted rows through normal read.
Response contract: Returns active branding or approved absence state with fallback indicators logo relationship summary and audit-safe timestamps.
Error contract: 400 invalid tenant id; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 tenant not found; 409 deleted branding not visible through normal read.
Cross-feature seams: tenants selected-tenant lookup; assets metadata summary for current logo when present
Persistence impact: Reads tenant branding durable record and current logo relationship.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique active branding record per tenant; indexes on tenant id deletedAt updatedAt and current logo asset id.
Search / filter model: Exact read by tenant id only in v1.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Normal reads exclude soft-deleted branding rows.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Cleanup failures may be included as maintenance-safe status only if approved.
Authorization enforcement layer: tenantBranding feature enforces selected-tenant and root capability; assets enforces asset invariants for logo metadata.
Audit requirement: Audit denied reads; successful reads optional unless security review requires.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; display name and logo metadata may reveal tenant identity.
Data classification / PII posture: Tenant branding metadata is customer/tenant configuration data.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when root reads are tenant-exact active-only and do not expose raw bucket authority.

Business goal: Allow a root admin to persist durable display name and primary colour for one tenant.
Tenant context rule: Root write identifies one selected tenant; request-body tenant inference is not authority.
Authorization summary: Root actor must hold manage capability for selected tenant; non-root and cross-tenant actors deny.
Request contract: Route param is exact tenant id; body allows branding display name and primary colour only; system-managed fields are rejected.
Response contract: Returns saved branding with generated ids timestamps fallback indicators and current logo relationship summary.
Error contract: 400 invalid colour empty display name or system-managed field; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 tenant not found; 409 soft-deleted branding conflict; 422 validation failure.
Persistence impact: Creates or updates active tenant branding record and refreshes updatedAt.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique active branding record per tenant; validation on normalized tenant id and colour format.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Soft delete if later approved sets deletedAt and refreshes updatedAt; v1 normal save does not update soft-deleted records.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Not applicable for non-expiring branding values.
Orphaned external resource handling: Not applicable unless logo relationship is changed.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: No scheduler dependency for display name or colour.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Not applicable for display name or colour.
Authorization enforcement layer: tenantBranding feature enforces root capability validation and lifecycle; tenants remains canonical tenant identity owner.
Audit requirement: Audit successful create/update and denied writes.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; branding display name may be customer-identifying.
Data classification / PII posture: Tenant branding display name and colour are durable tenant configuration facts.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when durable branding facts persist separately from canonical tenant name and successful saves refresh updatedAt.

Business goal: Allow a root admin to start a constrained tenant logo upload for one selected tenant.
Tenant context rule: Root write identifies one selected tenant; upload intent tenant scope must match branding owner.
Authorization summary: Root actor must hold branding logo update and asset create capabilities; assets validates upload invariants.
Request contract: Route param is exact tenant id; body declares content type byte size optional checksum and accessibility intent metadata; storage keys are server generated.
Response contract: Returns asset id upload intent id upload target expiry and accepted constraints without permanent bucket URL.
Error contract: 400 invalid MIME size checksum or metadata; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized or tenant mismatch; 409 quota or lifecycle conflict; 422 unsupported asset constraints.
Cross-feature seams: assets createAssetUploadIntent seam; tenants selected-tenant lookup
Persistence impact: Creates pending asset/upload-intent records in assets and may record pending branding logo relationship intent if approved.
Indexes / uniqueness: Assets owns upload-intent indexes; tenantBranding may index pending logo relationship by tenant id.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Upload intents are short-lived single-use actor-bound scope-bound and storage-key-bound.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Expired intents cannot become current logo; retry creates new intent and storage key.
Orphaned external resource handling: Abandoned objects follow assets cleanup semantics.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: Assets cleanup support command or future scheduler handles expired pending uploads.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Failed cleanup remains quota-visible and retryable through assets status.
Authorization enforcement layer: tenantBranding authorizes entity relationship first; assets enforces asset-native upload constraints second.
Audit requirement: Audit intent creation success denial quota denial and repeated mismatch attempts.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; filenames metadata and logo image may identify tenant.
Data classification / PII posture: Logo is tenant configuration asset with contextual accessibility metadata.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when logo upload intent is constrained by tenant branding authorization and asset invariants.

Business goal: Allow a root admin to replace the current tenant logo only with a consumer-ready asset relationship.
Tenant context rule: Selected tenant must match branding owner and asset tenant; cross-tenant link denies.
Authorization summary: Root actor must hold branding logo update and asset link/read capabilities; tenantBranding validates relationship before assets content is consumed.
Request contract: Route param is exact tenant id; body supplies asset id plus alt text or decorative posture; no clear/remove operation in v1.
Response contract: Returns updated logo relationship with readiness state fallback indicators and prior logo lifecycle posture.
Error contract: 400 missing accessibility metadata invalid asset id or clear request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized or tenant mismatch; 404 asset or tenant not found; 409 asset not ready rejected deleted cleanup-pending or incompatible; 422 sanitizer or metadata requirement unmet.
Persistence impact: Creates or updates current logo relationship on tenant branding and records prior asset dereference posture.
Indexes / uniqueness: One current logo relationship per active tenant branding record; indexes on tenant id asset id lifecycle and deletedAt.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Replacement creates a new current relationship; prior bytes remain under retention cleanup and audit rules.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Pending rejected deleted not-ready and metadata-incomplete assets cannot become consumer-ready.
Orphaned external resource handling: Prior and abandoned assets remain governed by assets cleanup and retention rules.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: Assets cleanup support command or future scheduler handles orphaned pending assets.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Failed cleanup remains quota/cost visible until successful or policy changes.
Authorization enforcement layer: tenantBranding owns relationship authorization; assets owns asset readiness invariants.
Audit requirement: Audit link replacement mismatch failure quota denial cleanup failure and denied cross-tenant attempts.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; logo and alt text may reveal customer identity.
Data classification / PII posture: Logo relationship metadata is tenant configuration data and may include accessibility text.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when only ready matching assets with contextual accessibility metadata can become current logo.

Business goal: Serve current tenant logo bytes through authorized same-origin delivery.
Capability boundary: tenant dashboard current tenant or root selected tenant
Tenant context rule: Tenant read evaluates one current tenant context matching branding owner and asset tenant; root read uses selected tenant authorization.
Authorization summary: Actor must be authorized by tenant branding relationship read before assets content read; public delivery is denied in v1.
Request contract: No mutable body; current tenant or selected tenant context is server-side authority.
Response contract: Returns same-origin image stream with safe content type and nosniff or returns typed not-available state through projection route.
Error contract: 400 invalid context; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized tenant mismatch or public access; 404 no current logo; 409 logo not ready metadata incomplete deleted rejected cleanup-pending or sanitizer-blocked.
Cross-feature seams: assets readAssetContent seam; tenant auth current context; root selected-tenant context
Persistence impact: Reads branding logo relationship and asset metadata; no branding mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on tenant id current logo asset id lifecycle and asset readiness status.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Content reads require ready consumer-ready logo relationship; normal reads exclude deleted assets and deleted branding.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Pending rejected expired and metadata-incomplete logos are not served.
Orphaned external resource handling: Missing storage object should produce typed failure and maintenance signal.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: No scheduler dependency for normal read.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Storage drift or cleanup failure should be recorded through assets maintenance posture.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated tenant session or root-admin session.
Authorization enforcement layer: tenantBranding enforces entity relationship and tenant context first; assets enforces content-read invariants second.
Audit requirement: Audit denied content reads; successful reads may be sampled or audited if security review requires.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; logo content may reveal customer identity.
Data classification / PII posture: Private tenant branding image content; no public delivery in v1.
Traceability status: Story AC-S004-03 AC-S005-01 AC-S008-03; first draft
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when logo bytes are served only after tenant branding authorization and through same-origin nosniff delivery.

Business goal: Return safe branding values for the authenticated tenant dashboard shell.
Tenant context rule: Exactly one current tenant context is required; wrong or missing tenant context denies.
Authorization summary: Tenant actor must be authorized for tenant dashboard branding read in current tenant; asset content is not authority by itself.
Request contract: No mutable body; current tenant context comes from server-side auth/session context.
Response contract: Returns display name primary colour logo URL or null accessibility posture fallback indicators and login/reload timing metadata.
Error contract: 400 missing current tenant; 401 unauthenticated; 403 cross-tenant denied; 404 tenant not found; 409 branding not consumable state; 503 projection dependency unavailable.
Cross-feature seams: tenant auth current tenant context; assets logo readiness/content route; tenants canonical name fallback
Persistence impact: Reads tenant branding record tenants canonical name fallback and logo relationship; no mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index active branding by tenant id; logo relationship lookup by current tenant.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Projection uses approved fallback values and does not promise live update to already-open dashboards.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Cleanup failure may cause logo null fallback and operational status if approved.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated tenant session with current tenant context.
Authorization enforcement layer: tenantBranding enforces tenant current-context read and cross-tenant deny.
Audit requirement: Audit denied projection reads and dependency failures if security review requires.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; projection exposes tenant display identity and logo URL to authorized tenant users.
Data classification / PII posture: Tenant dashboard branding projection is tenant-scoped configuration data.
Traceability status: Story AC-S005-01 AC-S005-02 AC-S005-03 AC-S008-01 AC-S008-02; first draft
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when dashboard receives safe fallback-aware branding for exactly one current tenant after login or reload.

Business goal: Record reviewable security privacy and lifecycle evidence for branding and logo operations.
Tenant context rule: Root and tenant operations record actor tenant operation outcome and safe metadata without secrets or storage credentials.
Authorization summary: Audit writer records success denial mismatch failure cleanup quota and cross-tenant outcomes for approved events.
Route(s): Internal audit writer seam and any future audit read routes
Request contract: Event payload includes actor tenant operation result reason safe ids and timestamps; forbidden fields include raw bytes storage credentials upload targets tokens and bearer/session identifiers.
Response contract: Audit records are durable and queryable through approved audit views when those views exist.
Error contract: 400 invalid event payload; 403 unauthorized audit read if surfaced; 409 audit writer unavailable or retry needed; 422 forbidden field detected.
Cross-feature seams: audit event writer; assets audit posture
Persistence impact: Creates audit events and may record cleanup failure retry metadata.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on tenant id actor id event type createdAt and operation result if audit storage is added or extended.
Search / filter model: Audit lookup only through approved audit surfaces.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Audit records persist according to retention policy and do not make failed cleanup invisible.
Expiry / abandoned-state behavior: Failed cleanup records remain visible and count against limits until resolved or policy changes.
Orphaned external resource handling: Cleanup failures and quota denials remain operationally visible.
Scheduled maintenance or job dependency: Future support command or scheduler may retry cleanup through assets; audit records failure and retry outcomes.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Failed cleanup reason and retry status are durable.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated feature service context or approved audit viewer for reads.
Authorization enforcement layer: Feature emits audit-safe events; audit feature controls read authorization if surfaced.
Audit requirement: Audit is mandatory for privileged and denied operations.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; event metadata may identify tenant actor and asset relationships.
Data classification / PII posture: Audit data is security-sensitive operational metadata.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when required events are recorded without forbidden fields and cleanup failures remain visible.

Business goal: Ensure root-admin branding and tenant dashboard branding consume governed design-system seams.
Tenant context rule: Root-admin surface uses selected tenant; tenant dashboard surface uses current tenant context.
Authorization summary: Frontend visibility follows backend capabilities and does not infer asset authority from asset ownership.
Route(s): Root-admin branding page and tenant dashboard shell routes to be finalized
Request contract: Frontend consumes projection and route contracts; no client-supplied system-managed fields; no app-page CSS.
Response contract: Renders form upload status colour preview validation fallback and dashboard branding states from approved design-system composition.
Error contract: Validation failure denied state unavailable projection missing logo not-ready logo rejected logo consumer-not-ready logo and cross-tenant-denied fallback.
Cross-feature seams: design-system form/upload/image/choice/drawer/list/page-shell/context-nav seams; root-admin topology; tenant dashboard shell
Search / filter model: UI filters not applicable in v1.
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Frontend reflects backend lifecycle states and does not create hidden durable state.
Cleanup retry and failure recording: Frontend displays cleanup or retry status only when API contract approves it.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated root-admin or tenant browser session depending on surface.
Authorization enforcement layer: Backend remains authority; frontend gates visibility and handles denied states honestly.
Audit requirement: Frontend does not create audit events except through backend operations.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; logo and display name visible to authorized users.
Data classification / PII posture: Rendered branding is tenant-scoped configuration presentation.
Traceability status: Story AC-S002-01 AC-S002-02 AC-S007-01 AC-S007-02 AC-S007-03 AC-S008-01 AC-S008-02; first draft
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when app UI consumes signed-off design-system composition without app-page CSS copied markup or duplicated controller behavior.

Business goal: Keep source-independent artifacts aligned before Delivery starts.
Tenant context rule: Not applicable; planning artifacts record root and tenant boundaries before source changes.
Authorization summary: Artifact owners must update PRD matrix API data permission design-system asset test blueprint manifest and generated graph surfaces before implementation closes.
Response contract: Maintained artifacts exist and reference each other by stable ids.
Error contract: Validation errors stale artifacts or generated graph drift block handoff.
Cross-feature seams: change-control standards; feature manifest workflow; generated dependency graph
Lifecycle / cleanup rules: Artifact lifecycle follows change-control status and supersession rules.
Authorization enforcement layer: Change-control validation and review enforce completeness.
Audit requirement: Audit not applicable beyond repo history and review notes.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; planning artifacts avoid secrets credentials tokens storage keys and raw uploaded content.
Acceptance notes: Acceptable when downstream artifacts are coherent and stale source-independent docs do not describe pre-change truth.
